key_insight: Machine-learning models compress quantum measurement data to supply wavefunction overlaps efficiently, accelerating quantum-classical Monte Carlo by orders of magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Reusing learned quantum-state information reduces classical measurement-processing overhead, improving the scalability of hybrid quantum simulations.
method: Prepare trial wavefunctions on a quantum processor.
Compress quantum measurement data into machine-learning models.
Use predicted wavefunction overlaps to guide classical quantum Monte Carlo.
evidence_signal: Using measurements from Google's Willow processor, the authors report chemically accurate simulations of hydrogen chains and strongly correlated iron-sulfur clusters on up to 40 qubits.
watch_item: Broader deployment requires validating that learned overlap errors remain controlled for new systems and quantum measurement conditions.
paper_title: Machine learning quantum data to accelerate quantum Monte Carlo
